issue.title: Bug: PDDF - If multiple agents are getting/setting LED color, there is a race condition.

failure.body:
### Is it platform specific

broadcom

### Importance or Severity

Low

### Description of the bug

PDDF - If multiple agents are getting/setting LED color, there is a race condition.

### Steps to Reproduce

On a PDDF platform calling [get_led_color_from_cpld](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/b228122f388ecfdde86ae6921a30f60b9d4d8900/platform/pddf/platform-api-pddf-base/sonic_platform_pddf_base/pddfapi.py#L158) or [set_led_color_from_cpld](https://github.com/sonic-net/sonic-buildimage/blob/b228122f388ecfdde86ae6921a30f60b9d4d8900/platform/pddf/platform-api-pddf-base/sonic_platform_pddf_base/pddfapi.py#L198) more multiple agents can cause a race condition.

As seen in the existing code below.

Each set_led_color_from_cpld requires writing to the following sysfs paths in one atomic operation.
```
/sys/kernel/pddf/devices/led/device_name
/sys/kernel/pddf/devices/led/index
/sys/kernel/pddf/devices/led/color
/sys/kernel/pddf/devices/led/dev_ops
/sys/kernel/pddf/devices/led/cur_state/color
```

Each get_led_color_from_cpld requires writing to the following sysfs paths in one atomic operation.
```
/sys/kernel/pddf/devices/led/device_name
/sys/kernel/pddf/devices/led/index
/sys/kernel/pddf/devices/led/dev_ops
/sys/kernel/pddf/devices/led/cur_state/color
```

```
    def set_led_color_from_cpld(self, led_device_name, color):
        index = self.data[led_device_name]['dev_attr']['index']
        device_name = self.data[led_device_name]['dev_info']['device_name']
        self.create_attr('device_name', device_name,  self.get_led_path())
        self.create_attr('index', index, self.get_led_path())
        self.create_attr('color', color, self.get_led_cur_state_path())
        self.create_attr('dev_ops', 'set_status',  self.get_led_path())
        return (True, "Success")
```

```
    def get_led_color_from_cpld(self, led_device_name):
        index = self.data[led_device_name]['dev_attr']['index']
        device_name = self.data[led_device_name]['dev_info']['device_name']
        self.create_attr('device_name', device_name,  self.get_led_path())
        self.create_attr('index', index, self.get_led_path())
        self.create_attr('dev_ops', 'get_status',  self.get_led_path())
        return self.get_led_color()
```

This will cause a race condition, if multiple agents are calling `set_led_color_from_cpld` and `get_led_color_from_cpld`, each call can get its sysfs files overwritten midway between able to finish the entire operation.

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

No race condition, can call the methods from multiple agent.

### Relevant log output

```shell
Errors like:

[  124.847956] PDDF_LED ERROR find_led_ops_data invalid index: 36 for type:FANTRAY_LED_1;3

In this case, one process was setting to index to 36 to operate on a port LED, while another process was attempting a fantray led operation.
```

### Output of `show version`, `show techsupport`

```shell

```

### Attach files (if any)

_No response_

resolution.title: [PDDF] Add file lock for led ctrl
resolution.description:
#### Why I did it
pddf uses a shared sysfs interface for getting/setting led status for all leds. Our system currently has 3 processes that gets/sets led status using the pddf api:
 - healthd
 - port-ledd.service
 - system-ledd.service

There's the potential for simultaneous sysfs operations to interfere with each other, resulting in errors like:
```
[  124.847956] PDDF_LED ERROR find_led_ops_data invalid index: 36 for type:FANTRAY_LED_1;3
```
This problem is not unique to our system. Any vendor using pddf for leds is susceptible to this.

Fixes #22699
